about.title: San Gabriel Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Gabriel sees a steady stream of injury collisions each year, with recent public records showing 155 injury crashes and 207 people hurt in a single year, plus two traffic deaths. Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. tend to bring more reported crashes, and corridors like Las Tunas Drive, Del Mar Avenue, and Valley Boulevard show up often in the collision counts. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, what happens in the days right after matters. Photos, witness names, and medical records fade or disappear fast, and insurance adjusters move quickly to lock in a recorded statement before you understand your injuries. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect injured San Gabriel residents, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, deal with the insurer, and help protect the record while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a city road or Metro bus, was involved. An attorney can spot that issue early instead of after it's too late.

items.title: Fault Isn't All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly blamed for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the amount. Insurers often try to shift blame onto you during a recorded statement, so it helps to have someone speaking for you.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get help evaluating your San Gabriel crash. You only pay a fee if the attorney recovers compensation on your behalf.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later, even if you're just trying to be cooperative. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: What if my crash happened on a street maintained by the city, like near San Gabriel Boulevard?
items.answer: Claims involving a government-owned road or vehicle, such as a city street or public bus, often carry a much shorter filing deadline than the standard two years, sometimes just six months. It's worth having an attorney check this quickly so you don't miss a critical deadline.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we're not a law firm ourselves. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
